intended_object: The set {(i, j) ∈ ι × ι : i < j} of strictly-above-diagonal positions of an ι×ι matrix. These index the free coordinates x_{ij} of the unitriangular group U_ι, whose coordinate ring is the polynomial ring K[x_{ij} : i < j]. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `FreeCoordinateRing := MvPolynomial (StrictUpperPair ι) K` and in `AffineSpace (StrictUpperPair ι) (Spec K)`.
explanation:
The body is the subtype `{p : ι × ι // p.1 < p.2}`, which is exactly the set of index pairs strictly above the diagonal. The library proves its cardinality is `(card ι).choose 2`, as expected. It is basically an index set for the coordinates. As a set it is the standard one, so there is nothing wrong with it.

On generality: the definition only uses `<`. The section's `[Fintype ι] [LinearOrder ι]` are the natural assumptions for unitriangular matrices indexed by a finite totally ordered set, which is the setting of the whole file. Asking for less here (only an `LT` instance) would not help anywhere. Mathlib has no dedicated declaration for this set of pairs. The nearest relative, `Matrix.BlockTriangular`, is a predicate on matrices, not an index type.
